title: SAVE keyword — explicit retention; without it, locals are 'undefined' on re-entry per F77 standard
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE TOTAL_TICK(DELTA, RUN)
C     RUN persists across calls via explicit SAVE. Without SAVE,
C     the F77 standard says RUN is 'undefined' after each RETURN.
C     IBM XL and most legacy compilers happened to give SAVE-like
C     behaviour anyway (stack-allocated locals stayed put), but
C     standards-conformant compilers may zero or scramble.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      REAL DELTA, RUN
      SAVE RUN
      RUN = RUN + DELTA
      RETURN
      END
notes: Explicit SAVE is the standard-correct way to keep state. The open question: what is the initial value? F77 says 'undefined'. Many compilers default to 0; many legacy code paths assume it. The spec must surface this so the rewrite explicitly initialises (e.g. RUN = 0.0 at module-init time).
